::: {.block title="Data leakage and split design"}
In situ samples are not independent. An OOI mooring gives eight 3 h windows a
day that share one daily satellite pixel, so a random 80/20 split puts
near-copies on both sides. We hold out whole 1° × 30-day blocks instead (space-time); new region holds out 10° boxes.
For BGC-Argo the split makes no difference. For OOI, almost all of the random
split's skill is leakage, and pooling Argo and OOI hides it in one number.
Split by space and time, and report platforms separately.

| Data | Split | 0–10 m | 50–60 m | 100–110 m | Integrated |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Argo | Random rows | 0.76 | 0.58 | 0.39 | 0.33 |
| | Space-time | 0.75 | 0.58 | 0.38 | 0.32 |
| | New region | 0.74 | 0.56 | 0.35 | 0.26 |
| OOI | Random rows | **0.89** | **0.79** | **0.82** | **0.80** |
| | Space-time | 0.54 | −0.01 | −0.09 | 0.18 |
| | New region | 0.10 | −0.24 | −0.74 | −0.36 |
| Argo + OOI | Random rows | 0.85 | 0.69 | 0.46 | 0.57 |
| | Space-time | 0.77 | 0.46 | 0.32 | 0.53 |
| | New region | 0.70 | 0.39 | 0.23 | 0.43 |

: R² of log10 Chl *a* by depth bin, and of integrated Chl *a*, on held-out data (mean of 5 repeats). {#tbl-leakage}
:::
